items.title: Africa's shifting role in the global drug trade
items.summary: Recent discoveries of meth labs suggest parts of Africa are moving beyond drug transit and becoming sites of synthetic drug production For years, Africa was primarily known as a transit point for international drug trafficking networks But recent drug seizures and laboratory discoveries show that illicit drugs are no longer only passing through African countries — they are increasingly being manufactured there Recent discoveries of methamphetamine laboratories in countries such as Nigeria , South Africa , Kenya and Mozambique have fueled concerns that Africa is becoming a significant production hub for synthetic drugs According to the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), synthetic drug production increasingly involves transnational criminal networks and clandestine laboratories capable of supplying both local and international markets The debate gained new urgency this year after Nigeria's National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) dismantled what the agency described as the largest clandestine methamphetamine laboratory ever uncovered in the country The operation in Nigeria's…

items.title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK
items.summary: DR Congo has been facing the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country's history A British man who has tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo will be flown back to the UK It is the first confirmed case of a UK national contracting Ebola during the most recent outbreak of the rare but deadly virus in DR Congo, which has so far led to more than 5,000 deaths It is not clear when the flight will take place Earlier, a UK government spokesperson said there were "well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this" and that the risk to the public remains low Reuters news agency reported the infected man is a healthcare worker, citing an internal document BBC News has not seen Imported Ebola cases are extremely rare in the UK and have resulted in no deaths There have only been four confirmed cases of the virus in the UK - one, in 1976, resulting from a laboratory incident, and three involving health workers who were responding to an outbreak in West Africa between 2014 and 2015 A UK government spokesperson said: "The UK has well-established procedures for…

items.title: Wawira Njiru, Kenya's school feeder and German Africa Prize recipient
items.summary: From a small fundraiser to a major enterprise, Wawira Njiru's Kenyan school feeding scheme has been more successful than she ever thought possible. She's now being awarded the German Africa Prize From starting a modest fundraiser for 25 school children, Wawira Njiru, 35, has become a social entrepreneur with a staggering 6,000 staff on her payroll, feeding 600,000 kids in Kenya every day with her organization Food4Education (F4E), an engagement for which she is being honored with this year's German Africa Prize . How did this transformation come to pass? The answer may be in her character. Stubborn and hardworking, that's how Njiru sees herself. "It's hard to tell me something is not possible." Thinking back to how she began, she explained, "My dream then, my ambition was to feed 100 kids every day.

items.title: Democrats take House and Senate from Republicans in US midterm rout
items.summary: Democrats will control both chambers of Congress after flipping seats in Republican strongholds across the US in an election seen as a repudiation of President Donald Trump By late Tuesday night, it was clear that Democrats had succeeded in turning the 2026 US midterm elections into the so-called "blue wave" that had been predicted by pollsters But by Wednesday morning, the scale of the victory had turned into a "blue tsunami," surprising even the most optimistic political pundits In January, Democrats are set to have a commanding majority of at least 237 to 139 in the House and a 54 to 44 advantage in the Senate Democratic candidates flipped seven highly competitive Senate seats, including in what have for decades been reliably Republican districts in "red" states Texas voted in James Talarico as its first Democratic Senator since 1988, while electing a Democratic governor, Gina Hinojosa, for the first time in over 30 years The heartland state of Kansas, where farmers have been hit by high diesel prices and tariffs, will send a Democrat, Adam Hamilton, to the US Senate for the…

items.title: US midterm results a 'victory' for Canadians hopeful of tariff relief

items.title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline
items.summary: More than 500 parties are contesting the elections South Africans are voting in highly contested local elections likely to see a haemorrhaging of votes for the country's biggest party, the African National Congress (ANC) This year's voting season has been marked by intense campaigns that have included politicians spinning cars, watching grannies knit and even wading through giant-sized potholes Election officials say voting is going smoothly, despite long queues at some polling stations Leaders are campaigning to head South Africa's nearly 300 municipalities, responsible for basic service provision such as water, electricity and refuse collection For the ANC, the elections are a chance to prove it still has what it takes to govern.
